mainTopic: The layout of a family burial cave (niches, chambers and courtyard), and the גמרא's question about where רבי שמעון's two entrance niches are dug.
overview: The amud opens in the middle of a משנה about the family burial cave a buyer is entitled to. It finishes the size of each burial niche (כוך), which is six טפחים wide. רבי שמעון gives a larger burial chamber: 6 by 8 אמות with 13 niches, including one on each side of the entrance. The משנה then describes a 6-by-6 courtyard (חצר) in front of the chambers, big enough for the bier and its bearers. The תנא קמא says two chambers open onto the courtyard, while רבי שמעון says four. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says it all depends on the strength of the rock. The גמרא asks where רבי שמעון's two entrance niches can go, since digging them under the courtyard would mean people walk on the graves, and a משנה treats the courtyard as טהור. רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא answers that they are cut upright like a door bolt, and the גמרא begins a challenge from רבי יוחנן that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Finishing the measurements of each burial niche
steps.stepSummary: The משנה finishes its list of measurements for a burial niche (כוך): the width is six טפחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And their width is six handbreadths.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is finishing a sentence it began just before this section, giving the last measurement of the burial niches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this line, the משנה gave the length and height of each כוך. Here it adds the width: six טפחים. That completes the picture of a single niche before the משנה turns to the chamber as a whole.

keyTerms.meaning: a burial niche dug into the cave wall / niches

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the units. This 'six' means six טפחים (handbreadths). The cave and courtyard measurements that come next are in אמות (cubits), which are much bigger.

phrases.notes: 'Their' means the burial niches, and the six is in טפחים (handbreadths).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the תנא קמא's measurements of a niche, which began just before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each burial niche is six טפחים wide.

steps.title: רבי שמעון's layout for the burial chamber
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון says the burial chamber is 6 by 8 אמות with 13 niches: four on each long wall, three on the wall facing the entrance, and one on each side of the entrance.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: He makes the inside of the cave six cubits by eight, and opens thirteen niches into it: four on this side, four on that side, three facing them, one to the right of the entrance and one to the left.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון gives a different and larger layout for the burial chamber than the one the משנה described before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra size lets the chamber hold 13 niches. Four go along each long wall and three go on the far wall opposite the entrance. רבי שמעון also adds one niche on each side of the entrance itself, using the entrance wall as well.

phrases.english: He makes the inside of the cave
and opens into it thirteen niches:
four from here and four from there,

phrases.notes: These go on the far wall, opposite the entrance.

phrases.english: and one to the right of the entrance,

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: עוֹשֶׂה תּוֹכָהּ שֶׁל מְעָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the תנא קמא's layout of the chamber and its niches.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי שמעון, the chamber is 6 by 8 אמות and has 13 niches.

steps.title: The courtyard at the cave entrance
steps.stepSummary: A courtyard of 6 by 6 אמות is made at the cave entrance, big enough for the bier and the people burying the dead.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he makes a courtyard at the entrance of the cave, six by six, the size of the bier and those who bury him.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves from the inside of the chamber to the open courtyard (חצר) in front of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה explains why it is 6 by 6: that is enough room for the bier together with the people carrying it. This way the burial can be done comfortably at the cave entrance.

keyTerms.meaning: bier (the bed the dead person is carried on)

phrases.english: And he makes a courtyard at the entrance of the cave
the full size of the bier and those who bury it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the תנא קמא's description after רבי שמעון's interjection, moving from the chamber to the courtyard outside it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The courtyard at the cave entrance is 6 by 6 אמות, enough room for the bier and its bearers.
steps.whyThisMatters: The size is tied to a practical need: having enough room to carry out a burial.

steps.title: How many chambers open onto the courtyard
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא says two burial chambers open onto the courtyard, one on each side. רבי שמעון says four, one on each of its four sides.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he opens two caves into it, one from here and one from there. רבי שמעון says: four, on its four sides.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה says how many burial chambers branch off the courtyard, and רבי שמעון disagrees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the תנא קמא, the courtyard has two chambers on opposite sides. רבי שמעון, who already gave each chamber more niches, also gives the courtyard more chambers: one on every side, four in all.
steps.whatToRemember: The whole layout: niches (כוכין) are dug into a chamber (מערה), and the chambers open onto a shared courtyard (חצר). Wherever רבי שמעון disagrees, he gives a larger version than the תנא קמא: a bigger chamber, 13 niches, and four chambers instead of two. He does not dispute the size of the courtyard.

phrases.english: And he opens two caves into it:
one from here and one from there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Describes what opens onto the courtyard from step 3, followed by רבי שמעון's disagreement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תנא קמא says two chambers open onto the courtyard. רבי שמעון says four, one on each side.

steps.title: Everything depends on the rock
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says the layout of the niches depends on how strong the rock is.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: everything depends on the rock.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with a third opinion. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says there is no fixed layout, because it all depends on the rock.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא and רבי שמעון gave exact numbers for chambers and niches. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says those numbers are not fixed. Hard rock can hold more niches packed closer together, and soft rock needs fewer niches with more space between them.

keyTerms.meaning: Rock, the bedrock the cave is cut into

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה gives exact sizes, but רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says the real layout depends on how strong the rock is.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third opinion to the dispute over the burial cave's layout.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The number and spacing of niches depend on the strength of the bedrock.

steps.title: Which way do the two entrance niches point?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which direction רבי שמעון's two niches beside the entrance are dug.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: These two niches, which way does he dig them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and asks about the two niches next to the entrance in רבי שמעון's plan. This question sets up the problems that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The other niches go straight back into the rock walls. The two niches beside the entrance are on the same wall as the doorway. Behind that wall is the courtyard, so it is unclear where these niches can go.

phrases.english: These two, in which direction does he set them?
phrases.notes: These are the two niches from step 2, one on each side of the entrance.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the משנה to a practical question about רבי שמעון's layout.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The direction in which the two niches beside the entrance are dug.

steps.title: Outward niches would be walked on
steps.stepSummary: If the niches ran outward under the courtyard, people would walk over the dead.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they point outward, people will trample over them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the obvious option, that the niches run outward under the courtyard floor. It rejects that option because people would walk on top of the graves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone walks through the courtyard to bring in the dead. Graves dug under its floor would be stepped on all the time, and that is disrespectful to the dead.

phrases.notes: Outside the chamber means into the courtyard, under its floor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rules out one possible answer to the question.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the entrance niches run outward under the courtyard.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: People walking through the courtyard would step over the dead, which is not respectful.

steps.title: A משנה says the courtyard is pure
steps.stepSummary: A משנה says a person standing in a burial courtyard is טהור, so there cannot be graves under it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Furthermore, we learned: in the courtyard of a burial cave, one who stands inside it is pure!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second, stronger problem from a משנה. The משנה treats the courtyard as free of the dead, so niches cannot run under it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Standing over a dead body makes a person טמא. The משנה says someone in the burial courtyard is טהור, which assumes no body lies under the courtyard. Niches dug outward would go against that assumption.

keyTerms.meaning: But we learned in a משנה
The courtyard in front of a burial cave

steps.confusionAlert: This is not saying the courtyard has a special purity rule. The courtyard is טהור simply because no dead body is under it.

phrases.english: the courtyard of a burial cave,
one who stands inside it is pure!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second objection to the outward option.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the entrance niches run outward under the courtyard.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה rules that someone standing in the courtyard is טהור. That ruling assumes no dead body is under the courtyard.

steps.title: The niches are dug like a door bolt
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא says the two niches are dug like a door bolt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: He makes them like a kind of door bolt.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא answers the question. The niches do not run out under the courtyard. They are cut beside the doorway, shaped like a bolt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A door bolt slides along the side of the door. In the same way, these niches are cut alongside the entrance, standing up and down, so the dead are buried upright. Nothing lies under the courtyard, so both problems go away.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, said:
He makes them like a kind of door bolt.
phrases.notes: Picture the niche going straight up and down beside the doorway, the way a bolt sits along a door.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא דְּעָבֵיד לְהוּ כְּמִין נֶגֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in a way that avoids both objections.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the shape of the niche
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The niches would have to run outward under the courtyard.
steps.terutzMaskana: The niches are cut upright beside the entrance, like a bolt, so nothing is under the courtyard.

steps.title: A challenge from רבי יוחנן begins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts to challenge the door-bolt answer with a statement of רבי יוחנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge to רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא. The words of רבי יוחנן's statement come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word והא signals a challenge against the answer just given. Since the door-bolt answer means burying someone upright, רבי יוחנן's statement will be about upright burial.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't he say? This opens a challenge

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a challenge to the door-bolt answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's door-bolt explanation
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A statement of רבי יוחנן about burying the dead upright will be brought against it. Its content comes in the next line.
